A2.note: Valid WIT plus valid HTTP signature to a granted workload is accepted; Maurice decides (cases.json:5).

A3.note: Server not supporting response signing MUST return 501 with problem type wimse-signed-response-unsupported.

A4.note: Valid WIT plus valid WPT is accepted.

A5.note: No WIMSE signature and no WPT: http-signature-08 defines no error for an absent signature; 401+WWW-Authenticate: WPT is only a wpt-02 s2.1 SHOULD for WPT-related rejects, and http-signature-08 s3.6 calls 401 NOT RECOMMENDED.

A6a.note: No draft says what a receiver does with an extra X-API-Key header; 400 is Maurice's behaviour (journal reason mixed-credentials).

A6b.note: Receiver check 'exactly one Authorization header field ... WPT scheme'; Bearer alongside WPT is rejected; 400 or 401 both accepted by the case.

A12a.note: Ed25519 is the fully-specified alg used in the draft examples; valid proof must be accepted (HTTP-sig).

A12b.note: EdDSA is the deprecated alias; creds-03 s5.1 only requires an IANA-registered alg and http-sig s3.1 lets the recipient reject algs 'not acceptable under local policy', so accepting EdDSA is Maurice policy (HTTP-sig).

A12c.note: Ed25519 is the fully-specified alg used in the draft examples; valid proof must be accepted (WPT).

A12d.note: EdDSA is the deprecated alias; creds-03 s5.1 only requires an IANA-registered alg and http-sig s3.1 lets the recipient reject algs 'not acceptable under local policy', so accepting EdDSA is Maurice policy (WPT).

A13a.note: Identifier with no path MUST be rejected (path required / no dot segments, decoded or literal); 400 from http-signature-08 s3.6.

A13b.note: Identifier with "./" segment MUST be rejected (path required / no dot segments, decoded or literal); 400 from http-signature-08 s3.6.

A13c.note: Identifier with "../" segment MUST be rejected (path required / no dot segments, decoded or literal); 400 from http-signature-08 s3.6.

A13d.note: Identifier with %2E%2E segment (decodes to a dot segment) MUST be rejected (path required / no dot segments, decoded or literal); 400 from http-signature-08 s3.6.

A13e.note: Identifier MUST NOT contain port; 400 from http-signature-08 s3.6 (case also tolerates untrusted-trust-domain as the reason).

A13f.note: Identifier MUST NOT contain query; 400 from http-signature-08 s3.6.

A13g.note: Identifier MUST NOT contain fragment; 400 from http-signature-08 s3.6.

A13h.note: Identifier MUST NOT contain userinfo; 400 from http-signature-08 s3.6 (case also tolerates untrusted-trust-domain as the reason).

A13i.note: Host case and decoded unreserved %7E follow from RFC 3986 s6.2.2 normalization, which the draft requires; the draft does not mention %7E literally; the grant table itself is Maurice config.

A13j.note: Draft says %2F MUST remain encoded in comparison so /a%2Fb is a different identifier, but the 403 comes from Maurice's grant table (not-authorized).

C2.note: Signature must verify with the key in WIT cnf; mismatch is a failed request authentication, 400.

C3.note: Recipients 'MAY maintain a replay cache and SHOULD reject' a seen nonce; strength is SHOULD, not MUST.

C4.note: wimse-aud MUST match the recipient's trusted audience values; failure is 400.

C4b.note: Audience comparison is Simple String Comparison, so a trailing slash is a mismatch.

C11.note: A credential MUST be validated only against anchors bound to its trust domain; unknown trust domain fails (400).

C12.note: Draft supports not resolving iss ('validators are not required to use iss'), but the refusal reason issuer-not-allowed is Maurice's iss allowlist (cases.json C12, no_fetch_port).

C12b.note: Trust entry without iss allowlist: outcome (400 or 403, three accepted reasons) depends on Maurice's trust configuration; only the no-fetch check is draft-backed.

IN4.note: Expired validity window is an authentication failure; 400.

IN6.note: iss is RECOMMENDED-but-optional and validators are not required to use it; the allowlist is Maurice config.

IN10.note: Receiver MUST verify Content-Digest; mismatch is 400.

IN11.note: 'If more than one signature has that tag value, the recipient MUST reject the message.'

IN12.note: keyid MUST NOT be used (sender rule); recipient rejection with 400 is inferred from s3.6 'malformed data structure'.

IN13.note: WPT alg MUST match cnf jwk alg; 401+WWW-Authenticate: WPT is wpt-02 s2.1 SHOULD but conflicts with http-signature-08 s3.6 (400, 401 NOT RECOMMENDED); our own peers/wimse.py:422 treats Ed25519/EdDSA as equal so would accept this input.

IN15.note: Authorization of a valid identity is Maurice's grant table; no draft defines it.

B_CHAIN.note: Normal-path 9-hop run; only hop 2 (Maurice :5050, chain_driver.py:145-175) is an independent decider, all other signers/verifiers are peers/wimse.py on both ends.

C5.note: Txn-Token MUST be signed when present, so swapping it breaks the signature; both signer and verifier are peers/wimse.py (domain_b.py:560). Peer returns distinct reason in body, see contradictions.

C6.note: 'A Txn-Token MUST NOT be accepted outside the Trust Domain identified by the aud claim'; 403 code is ours; the driver also blocks the send client-side (chain_driver.py:77-90).

C7.note: tctx is RECOMMENDED and application-defined; refusal comes from the file tool comparing tctx.file (domain_b.py:628); the 'injection' is a follow_injection flag in a scripted agent (domain_b.py:486), no LLM.

C8.note: Same mechanism as C7: scripted follow_injection request refused by tctx.file mismatch; no credential-exfiltration logic beyond checking 'eyJ' not in caller_context (domain_b.py:487).

C9.note: File tool route policy: /files/read requires a Txn-Token (domain_b.py:599); no draft defines delegated-only routes.

C9b.note: File tool route policy: /files/index forbids a Txn-Token (domain_b.py:605); no draft defines autonomous-only routes.

C10.note: Revocation is driven by our /admin/revoke endpoint (domain_b.py:536-545); creds-03 s9.3.1 'does not define a revocation mechanism for WITs'.

D1.note: Txn-Token header present but not in covered components violates 'MUST be signed when they exist'; both ends ours (wimse.py:389).

D2.note: tth MUST match the Txn-Token hash; 401+WWW-Authenticate: WPT is the wpt-02 SHOULD. File-tool hop is ours; an optional second hop to Maurice :5050 (chain_driver.py:702) is independent only when Maurice runs.

D3_exp.note: Downstream MUST verify the Txn-Token is not expired; 403 code is our choice.

D3_sig.note: Downstream MUST validate the JWS signature; 403 code is our choice.

D3_typ.note: typ MUST be txntoken+jwt; 403 code is our choice.

D3_reqwl.note: req_wl is REQUIRED; rejection on absence follows; 403 code is our choice (domain_b.py:591).

D3_dup.note: 'The value of this header MUST be exactly one Txn-Token'; the draft does not say what to do with two header lines, our file tool rejects (domain_b.py:554-558).

D4.note: Route requires scope files:read (domain_b.py:616); scope-to-route mapping is deployment policy.

D5.note: AS-B rejects typ at+jwt because it requires typ jwt-chg+jwt (domain_b.py:136-142), a typ the draft does not define; half of the scenario is a driver-side guard (chain_driver.py:1001-1024), not wire. Status 403 vs RFC 6749 s5.2/RFC 7523 s3.1 invalid_grant is unverified here.

D6.note: On the wire TTS-A issues four tokens (200); widened/mutated variants come from test_mode (domain_a.py:158-161) and are rejected by the driver helper (domain_a.py:425-452), not by a verifier on the wire.

D7.note: aud of the JWT grant MUST identify AS in trust domain B; wrong aud refused by AS-B (domain_b.py:140-149); 403 grant-invalid is our code, RFC 7523 s3.1 defers to RFC 6749 s5.2.
